summary: Admit verified Telegram channel-post webhooks through the existing tenant-bound Social Inbox/outbox boundary.

impacts.evidence: The public route resolves organization, workspace and account from the fixed callback path and checks the exact configured channel.
Only bounded normalized webhook identity and canonical event evidence cross the connector boundary; secrets and credentials remain ephemeral.
OpenAPI documents the public social webhook path and provider-specific verification headers.
Verified claims use the existing commerce.social.webhook_received.v1 event and host-owned outbox.
social.webhooks is an additive Telegram capability using the existing SocialWebhookReceiver interface.
Replay persistence uses the existing Task-009 Inbox and transactional outbox schema.
Secret-token constant-time verification, exact account/channel binding, bounded JSON and uniform public acknowledgement are independent gates.
Inbound receipt is not a privileged write operation and does not bypass approval policy.
Verified delivery identity is retained through the existing Inbox/outbox evidence path.
Content-addressed delivery claims are deduplicated by the tenant-scoped host processor.
The public route accepts only the Telegram verification header and delegates no caller-controlled egress.
Invalid and unavailable webhook deliveries are acknowledged uniformly and logged with bounded context.
Removing social.webhooks from runtime support disables Telegram receiver admission without rewriting stored evidence.
Connector, API route, runtime admission, OpenAPI, generated catalog and repository checks cover success, wrong secret, foreign channel and replay boundaries.
